result.title: FABLE task 001 / F1 — arithmetic transfer of the fixed symmetric-prime trial
result.status: mixed: normalization and leading-order S2 moments established (proved arithmetic asymptotic modulo recalled Selberg-Delange theorem, strong numerical confirmation); kernel derivation done as exact algebra; insertion-term (M2) transfer and completeness of M3 for all coincidences remain open, with a new finding that even the coincidence-free M2/alpha discreteness correction does not follow a clean O(1/log L) law out to L=1e8

claims.statement: F(s)=zeta(s)^a G(s) with C_ell=G(1)=prod_p(1-1/p)^a sum_e d_ell(p^e)^2 p^-e as stated; explicit Selberg-Delange Laurent coefficients kappa1=0.6588947, kappa2=0.1069575 derived from Stieltjes constants and G',G''
claims.evidence: f1_selberg_delange_expansion.py; f1_sd_expansion_results.json; mpmath cross-check of zeta'/zeta Laurent identities to 1e-9

claims.statement: Selberg-Delange (recalled theorem) gives a 3-term expansion of N(y)=sum_{n<=y} d_ell(n)^2/n; the 2-term numerical match improves from 4.7-13.5% (1-term) to 6e-3%-0.03% relative error at L=1e4..1e7
claims.status: proved arithmetic asymptotic (modulo recalled theorem) + finite numerical check

claims.statement: Marked Euler product identities for sum d_ell(n)^2 S~(n) n^-s and sum d_ell(n)^2 S~(n)^2 n^-s, with explicit next-order Laurent constants pi_0=-2.5434631, R1=2.3675580, R2=-0.0630942, derived by differentiating the theta-marked Euler product at theta=0
claims.evidence: f1_sd_expansion.py; one-line consequence of multiplicativity of d_ell(n)^2 and standard marked-product differentiation

claims.statement: Leading-order E_v[S2]=v^2/(a+1), E_v[S2^2]=(a+6)v^4/((a+1)(a+2)(a+3)) derived directly from the weighted integer sum via the marked Dirichlet series and Selberg-Delange, not assumed from a Poisson-Dirichlet model
claims.status: proved arithmetic asymptotic, leading order (modulo recalled Selberg-Delange theorem)
claims.evidence: section 3 of the report; matches Astra's stipulated moments exactly after v-derivative and C_ell(log L)^a cancellation

claims.statement: Numerical confirmation of F1-4's leading order is qualitatively present but the error rate has NOT stabilized at L<=1e7: rel.err*logL for the cumulative S2 and S2^2 ratios is still rising (0.207->0.502 and 1.605->1.944 across L=1e4..1e7 at v=1), and the corresponding 3-term Sigma_1,Sigma_2 expansions are also not yet stabilized (scaled residuals still drifting at x=1e7)
claims.status: finite numerical check; open regarding the true error rate

claims.statement: Exact correspondence beta<->M3 and alpha<->M2 (split between the off-diagonal piece of ||Ax||^2 and <x,A^2x>) derived directly from A's matrix entries A[qm,m]=2sin((pi/2)log q/log L)/(e sqrt q), via the standard (recalled) Mertens/PNT replacement of sums over primes by log-integrals

Exact 5-way finite decomposition alpha+beta+gamma+delta+eps=T (checked to <=1.2e-16 relative at every L); gamma (repeated p^2) decays like a clean 1/log L (ratio 2.53 over three decades vs predicted 2.00); delta (inserted prime divides background) is flat around 0.018 across L=1e3..1e6 with no visible decay; eps (prime powers e>=2) decays only by factor 1.34 (not 2) over three decades; alpha/D reaches only 49% of its claimed continuum limit M2/I even at L=1e6

Idealized coincidence-free model (exact continuum background, actual sum over primes instead of the integral) shows the alpha/M2 discreteness correction (alpha_semi-M2/I)*logL still moving by >3% per decade at L=1e8 (values -0.679,-0.784,-0.861,-0.920,-0.965,-1.000 for L=1e3..1e8); a single fixed-constant Mertens/logL correction (independently confirming the classical single-prime Mertens constant to 6e-5) is numerically off by nearly a factor of 2 at L=1e6; a post-hoc least-squares fit of the six points favors a log(log L)-type or 1/sqrt(log L)-type shape over plain 1/log L (max residuals 8.6e-3 and 3.6e-3 respectively vs 1.2e-2 and visibly curved for plain 1/log L)
claims.status: finite numerical check (the curve fit is diagnostic only, not a proof of the true rate)
claims.evidence: f1_prime_discreteness.py; f1_prime_discreteness_results.json; f1_prime_discreteness_run.log; inline least-squares fit done in this pass

claims.statement: Whether M3 already accounts for all leading diagonal coincidences, and whether the continuum schema's error term relative to the exact finite arithmetic sums is genuinely O(1/log L) at all (as opposed to a slower or differently-shaped rate such as log log L/log L), is not decided by any computation to date (L<=1e8)
claims.evidence: sections 5-7 of the report; no counterexample found at any tested L, but no proof of the assumed convergence rate either

claims.statement: The continuum schema (I, M2, M3, J as stipulated) is the correct leading arithmetic asymptotic of the underlying weighted integer sums, with a controlled, fully derived error term
claims.evidence: normalization and background S2-moments are established at leading order (F1-2, F1-4); the insertion-term (M2) transfer and coincidence completeness are not (F1-7, F1-8, F1-9); this is the strongest honest verdict, not a proof either way

unresolved: A two-prime (pair-correlation) Mertens/Selberg-Delange-type theorem for the double sum underlying the alpha/M2 term, with a genuine proved error term, has not been derived or cited; the log-log/1-over-sqrt(log L) curve fit in section 6 is diagnostic only.

Whether delta (inserted prime divides the background) and eps (prime powers e>=2) vanish at all relative to the leading term as L->infinity, and at what rate, is open; finite data through L=1e6 show delta flat and eps decaying much slower than a clean 1/log L law.
The fourth-order Selberg-Delange/Hankel coefficients of Sigma_1, Sigma_2 (needed to pin down the S2-moment error rate, which is still drifting at L=1e7) were not computed.
Inoue's Theorems 2 and 4 were not read (arxiv fetch blocked with EGRESS_BLOCKED, as in the prior F2 pass); every statement resting on them is labeled '(as described by Astra; paper not read)'.
The classical Selberg-Delange theorem itself was used as recalled, not independently re-proved or verified against a citation.
result.notes: This session resumed a partial run from earlier in the same overnight session (which had already hit a usage limit once): all six F1 scripts and their result/log files already existed in astra_tasks/task001/ when this pass began. I read every script and every result/log file in full, re-derived the key algebraic steps by hand to check them, cross-checked internal consistency (e.g. the cumulative-moment formula against the conditional-moment formula via integration, and the continuum J value against Astra's certified enclosure to ~20 digits via f1_continuum_results.json), ran one small inline least-squares fit on six already-computed numbers to test the shape of the slowest-converging residual (no new sieving or simulation), and wrote the final report. No pre-existing file was modified, nothing was committed, and no new large computation was run (all six scripts were already inside the ~20-minute budget when originally run: longest was f1_prime_discreteness.py at 88s, sieving primes to 1e8). Rules for this task explicitly allow reusing an already-present f1_moment_checks.py if found, which was the case. WebFetch of arxiv.org/html/2604.05733v1 was attempted once as instructed and blocked (EGRESS_BLOCKED), matching the F2 pass exactly. The most notable new finding beyond the already-completed F2 diagnostic is section 6: isolating the pure M2/alpha insertion term in an idealized model with the exact continuum background but the actual (discrete) sum over primes shows a discreteness correction that does not follow a clean single-constant O(1/log L) Mertens law out to L=1e8 -- this narrows the open question in a way that should let a future pass (or Astra) target a specific missing theorem (a two-prime Mertens/Selberg-Delange correlation estimate) rather than a vague "coincidence terms are large" observation.

result.title: r1 — CβE background bound: exponents, weakest link, numerics (task A3)
result.status: Deliverable written. Reuses Theorem B' verbatim. Parts (b),(c) proved modulo one clearly-named black box (BB-LD, local density control for general β) plus the cited Feng-Wei law; part (b) fully elementary as required; numerics (d) run successfully (9.9s, well under budget) with a β=2 validation against independent Haar CUE (KS p≈0.71).

claims.statement: CβE density Z^{-1}∏|e^{iθ_j}-e^{iθ_k}|^β is not determinantal/Pfaffian for β∉{1,2,4}; one-point density ρ_1≡N/2π exactly for all β by rotation invariance.

BB-LD (local near-diagonal n-point density control, the CβE analogue of the CUE file's exact Cauchy-Binet/Schur-function bound) is proved for β∈{1,2,4} via Pfaffian/determinantal structure but open for general β; identified as the single weakest link, reducing to quantitative Bourgade-Erdős-Yau-type local law/rigidity for circular β-ensembles (line-model version only currently recalled).
Clustering estimate P(δ_min ≤ L N^{-1-1/(β+1)} and ∃k∉{a,b} within c/N of the pair) ≤ κ_β L^{β+1} c^{2β+1}, generalizing r1_cue_background.md's L³c⁵ exactly at β=2 (β+1=3, 2β+1=5).
claims.evidence: §3, Prop 3.1'/3.2, Cor 3.3 (two false-start derivations left visible and diagnosed in §7 item 1)

claims.statement: Feng-Wei min-gap law: N^{1+1/(β+1)}δ_min converges in distribution to an explicit law, generalizing Ben Arous-Bourgade (β=2 recovers exponent 4/3).

The dyadic-shell stiffness bound (Lemma S) and window-stability lemma (Lemma W) of r1_theoremB_repair.md transfer to CβE verbatim for every β, since their proofs use only the elementary csc^2 bound and the unconditional gap ODE bound, with no β-dependence; part (b) is fully elementary as the task anticipated.

D_N^{CβE} ≍ N^{-2-2/(β+1)} in probability, modulo BB-LD, Feng-Wei, and Theorem B' (the last resolved via Corollary W2 using only static (H_C), arguably closing task A2's open item O1 as a side effect).

For general β, Yau-school DBM/local-relaxation-flow techniques are not merely cheaper than an explicit-density computation but are, to this file's knowledge, essentially the only known route to the clustering estimate, since no Weyl-dimension-type combinatorial identity exists for generic real β (unlike β=2's exact Schur/Cauchy-Binet machinery).

Numerics: Killip-Nenciu CMV construction verified unitary and eigenvalues unimodular to machine precision (~1e-15); β=2 instance matches an independently generated Haar CUE (Ginibre-QR) by two-sample KS test (stat 0.070, p=0.713 on both δ_min and S*); S*/N² median ≈0.13-0.14 across β=1,2,4, consistent with r1_cue_background.md's own CUE Monte Carlo; fitted δ_min exponent (N=64→128) 1.514 for β=1 (predicted 1.5) and 1.296 for β=4 (predicted 1.2), with the larger β=4 deviation consistent in direction with the slow finite-N convergence documented for CUE.
claims.evidence: §6, scripts/r1_cbe_mc.py, data/r1_cbe_mc.json, data/r1_cbe_mc.log; run took 9.9s wall time

unresolved: BB-LD (local density control at scale ~1/N for general β) is not established with an explicit, non-asymptotic constant in the literature recalled here; this is the single named weakest link.

A finite-N (non-asymptotic, Chebyshev-based) version of the Feng-Wei tail bound analogous to r1_cue_background.md's Proposition 3.3 was not derived; it would need BB-LD at n=2 and was deprioritized to fit the numerics into the time budget.

Larger N (256, 512) and larger sample counts were not run despite the 9.9s runtime showing ample budget remained; only the two N values (64,128) specified by the task were used for the exponent fit, which is consequently crude (2 points).
result.notes: Read r1_theoremB_repair.md and r1_cue_background.md in full before writing; reused Theorem B' and Lemma S/W verbatim without re-derivation as instructed. The determinantal toolkit of the CUE file (Cauchy-Binet, exact C_n(N)~N^{n^2} via Weyl dimension formula) does not generalize to general β since CβE is only determinantal/Pfaffian at β=1,2,4; this is the structural reason part (a) had to be reduced to a stated black box (BB-LD) rather than proved from scratch, as the task itself anticipated ("state and prove (or reduce to a precisely stated black box)"). The exponent-counting derivation in §3 required two corrective passes (left visible in the file, per this cluster's established convention of recording failed attempts rather than hiding them) because naively porting the CUE file's global N^9-type normalization constant onto BB-LD's locally-normalized (N/2π)^n statement produces a spurious residual N-power; the fix was to track normalizations consistently from BB-LD's definition, recovering the CUE file's L^{β+1}c^{2β+1} exponents exactly at β=2. Numerics used the Killip-Nenciu CMV/Verblunsky-coefficient model (recalled, not verified online), implemented from the standard OPUC block construction (Θ_j = [[ᾱ_j,ρ_j],[ρ_j,-α_j]], L=even blocks, M=⟨1⟩+odd blocks, C=LM); correctness was checked three ways (exact unitarity of C, exact unimodularity of eigenvalues, and internal consistency of two different S* formulas) all to ~1e-14-1e-15, plus an external cross-check at β=2 against an independently-built Haar CUE sample (Ginibre QR + Mezzadri correction) via two-sample KS test, which did not reject equal distributions (p≈0.71). Full run (250/200 samples, N=64,128) took 9.9s on one core, well under the 20-minute budget; nothing was shortened for time beyond capping N at 128 and not running a third N point, both flagged honestly in the unresolved list rather than silently limited.
